ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and clients against: (1) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (2) OFAC SDN List; (3) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (4) Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice Laws website; and (5) FINTRAC PEP / domestic-PEP guidance. Re-screening is required at onboarding, on every change in control or director appointment, and at least annually thereafter. Documentation must be retained in accordance with FINTRAC compliance program requirements (PCMLTFA s. 9.6) and CPATA ethical conduct rules; adverse hits must be escalated to the Alberta Registrar and the relevant Canadian competent authority.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (ACRS – Alberta Corporate Registration System), Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction; NUANS name search via authorized corporate registry service providers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in Latin-script English or French characters and consist of a distinctive element plus a mandatory corporate designator (Inc., Corp., Ltd., Incorporated, Limited, or French equivalents). Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. 'Patent Agent' and 'Trademark Agent' are restricted titles requiring CPATA licensure; federally incorporated names under the CBCA carry bilingual implications per s. 10 CBCA.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banker / Trust / Insurance / Credit Union
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the Registrar issues written reasons. Options: (1) file a revised name with a new NUANS report; (2) within 30 days submit a 'Request for Name Decision Review' to the Registrar of Companies, Service Alberta, with legal argument, the original NUANS report, trademark coexistence consents, and any regulator consents (e.g., CPATA or APEGA); (3) for restricted tokens, first obtain prior ministerial or regulatory approval; (4) if the rejection is upheld, apply for judicial review at the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 6 months under the Alberta Rules of Court; (5) for a federal CBCA name, appeal to the Director, Corporations Canada, under s. 12 CBCA.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the registered office (a physical registered address in Alberta is mandatory); however, CPATA professional-conduct rules require an actual business premises for client records, patent/trademark files, and FINTRAC/CRA scrutiny. A virtual mailbox alone is not acceptable for licensure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% probability of unannounced physical inspection in the first operating year; rising to 10%–15% if triggered by inconsistent GST/PST filings, non-resident UBO concentration, or FINTRAC/CRA compliance indicators.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 4(1), 6, 10(1), 21(1), 23, 24, 25(1), 108(2), 116(1) and 117(1)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form AB-1-1) submitted through the Alberta e-Registry system
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital required under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. Shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine under section 25. No escrow account or mandatory paid-up capital deposit applies to a Canadian-controlled private technology and IP prosecution corporation, provided the corporation qualifies as a private issuer.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the corporation hereby: (1) accepts the share capital as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation and issues subscription shares to the subscribers named in Schedule A for full consideration; (2) adopts the registered office and principal place of business located at the address set out in the Articles; (3) appoints the initial directors named in the Articles, each having filed a consent to act, to hold office until the first annual meeting of shareholders; and (4) appoints the officers of the corporation, being President, Treasurer, and Corporate Secretary, with full powers to execute banking authorities, regulatory filings, and routine corporate transactions. FURTHER RESOLVED that the officers are directed to complete and file the Certificate of Incorporation with the Alberta Corporate Registry and to undertake all necessary post-formation registrations, including business number, municipal, and professional licensing applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (Alberta e-Registry / NUANS search)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request with the proposed corporate name containing distinctive element and legal element ('Inc.' or 'Corp.'). Use e-Registry NUANS to obtain a name search report. If name is approved, reserve it for 90 days. Ensure no conflicting trademark or business name is found.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and alternate name list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged for conflict, submit an alternate distinct name or provide a letter of consent from the conflicting party, then re-file the NUANS request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Incorporation and By-Laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (via legal counsel or authorized agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act including corporate name, registered office address (physical, not P.O. box), share structure (authorized share classes, voting, preferences), restrictions on share transfers, number of directors, and first directors. Draft By-Law No. 1 covering management, meetings, officers, banking, and indemnification. Obtain director consents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the Articles or attachments, review the requisition notice, amend the documents to cure technical deficiencies, and resubmit within 14 calendar days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles of Incorporation with Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta e-Registry portal, Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed and signed Articles of Incorporation via the Alberta e-Registry portal or by paper filing. Pay the applicable incorporation filing fee. Receive the endorsed Certificate of Incorporation and endorsed Articles once processing is complete.
required_dossiers: Completed and executed Articles of Incorporation
NUANS name search report (if name reserved)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notice of defect is issued, file supplemental corrections or explanatory letters with Service Alberta. If rejected due to fee, re-pay and resubmit; if rejected due to name, switch to an alternate reserved name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Business Number and Tax Registrations with CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation and registered office details, register through CRA Business Registration Online or by telephone. Obtain the nine-digit Business Number (BN). Add program accounts: corporate income tax, GST/HST, payroll (RC), and any required excise accounts. Request a written confirmation of registration.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and mailing address
Business activity description (e.g. ISIC 7490 legal services / patent prosecution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA registration is delayed or queried, call CRA Business Enquiries, provide the incorporation certificate, correct any data-entry mismatches, and request a revised confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold First Board Meeting and Issue Shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the corporation (internal corporate record, minuted in Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors' meeting after the Certificate of Incorporation is issued. Adopt By-Law No. 1, approve share subscriptions, issue share certificates for the subscribed consideration, confirm the registered office, appoint officers, and authorize banking arrangements. All corporate minutes are entered in the corporation's records book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect in the meeting notice, quorum, or subscription terms is identified, ratify the resolution through a unanimous written resolution or hold a curative board meeting before financial records are filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Provincial, Municipal, and Professional Licensing Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry Service Alberta; Municipality (city business licence office); College of Patent Agents and Trademark Agents (CPATA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Update the Alberta Corporate Registry with annual return information. Apply for a municipal business licence or occupancy permit in the city where the registered office is located. If the corporation intends to operate as a patent prosecution agency, register the firm with CPATA and ensure each practising individual holds a valid patent agent or trademark agent licence.
required_dossiers: Office lease or proof of registered office location
Proof that individual patent/trademark agents are licensed under the College of Patent Agents and Trademark Agents Act
Workers' Compensation Board (WCB) employer account application (if employees are hired)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal licensing has zoning objections, provide evidence of professional office use or apply for a variance. If CPATA registration is incomplete, comply with the Registrar's deficiency letter by submitting missing declarations or revised professional liability insurance information.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: College of Patent Agents and Trademark Agents (CPATA), Office of the Registrar, Canada
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Patent Agent Firm Registration Certificate and Trademark Agent Firm Registration Certificate under the College of Patent Agents and Trademark Agents Act (S.C. 2018, c. 27)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (Government of Alberta) and, for federal matters, Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B Exemption — Office-only professional services. The proposed patent prosecution agency occupies no manufacturing or industrial site; the activity is not a 'designated project' under the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act, 2012, nor does it trigger a mandatory environmental impact assessment under Alberta's Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act. A self-assessment and records checklist are required, not a full EIA report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater or industrial effluent discharges from the office operation. Sanitary sewage must connect to the municipal sanitary sewer system and meet municipal sewer-use bylaws. HVAC and office operations must comply with applicable ventilation and building codes; no measurable volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from industrial processes are expected. Electronic waste, toner cartridges, and used batteries must be managed through Alberta's Recycling Regulation and hazardous waste requirements if generated; no on-site storage of hazardous materials is permitted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The corporation must obtain a fire safety inspection certificate or equivalent occupancy permit in accordance with the Alberta Fire Code, verify the structural load rating of the office premises for maximum workplace occupancy, register with the Alberta Workers' Compensation Board (WCB) for an employers account, maintain occupational health and safety compliance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code, and ensure the office workplace has adequate exits, fire extinguishers, and emergency procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – My Business Account portal at canada.ca/my-business-account; GST/HST program and Corporation Tax program administered federally; Alberta has no separate provincial corporate income tax or provincial sales tax administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Registry Requirements: Alberta Business Corporations Act incorporation or extra-provincial registration yields a Corporations Canada or Alberta Corporate Registry number. For tax identity, the reporting entity should apply for a 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) via the CRA 'Register a Business / Business Number (BN)' online service, paper RC1 form, or telephone. The BN is the master identifier; separate GST/HST account, payroll account, and corporate income tax account are linked to it. Foreign non-resident entities that carry on business in Canada or make taxable supplies in Canada must obtain a BN before filing any GST/HST return or corporate tax return. An Alberta-based corporation may complete the one-time CRA business registration and receive its BN immediately; subsequent accounts activated by request. No notarial filing is required for incorporation; foreign name reservations follow Alberta's regulations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada applies an entity-level federal income tax to corporations (Income Tax Act Part I) with provincial corporate tax allocated to Alberta at the corporate level; there is no 'check-the-box' partnership-style classification election available for corporations under Canadian tax law. Relevant statutory elections include: (i) association/control elections under ITA 256 to define associated corporations for the small business deduction; (ii) subsection 216(1) election for non-resident corporations with Canadian-source rental or timber income to file on net income basis instead of Part XIII withholding; (iii) GST/HST reg. election for exempt international services to zero-rate exporting services where the recipient is not subject to GST/HST; (iv) section 85 rollover election for incorporation/asset transfer; and (v) hybrid mismatch measures under ITA section 18.2 for excessive interest and financial arrangement rules (EIFEL). For a patent prosecution agency, the typical election is the GST/HST 'international services election' supporting zero-rating of exported IP prosecution services.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (annual worldwide taxable supplies threshold that triggers mandatory GST/HST registration under Excise Tax Act; once exceeded in any quarterly or annual calculation, registration is mandatory and applies prospectively).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federally mandated real-time e-invoice clearance or digital stamping. GST/HST invoices may be electronic in any format, provided the prescribed information in the Excise Tax Act is present: supplier BN, date, description, taxable amount, GST/HST payable, and stated tax in Canadian dollars. CRA audits retrieve source data, but no API clearance portal exists for transactional stamping. Alberta has no additional retail sales tax (no provincial levy), so GST 5% is the effective headline rate. Some IP prosecution services may be zero-rated exports, requiring proper documentation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods exported from Canada and to most services rendered to a non-resident recipient where the service is performed entirely outside Canada (or where the export is demonstrated and the recipient is not registered for GST/HST in Canada). For a patent prosecution agency, to zero-rate fees for international patent and trademark prosecution: the recipient must be a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST in Canada; the service must relate to foreign patent office proceedings or foreign registrations; and the service must not be supplied to a person present in Canada at the time. The Genuineness Test with EIFEL rules does not affect GST/HST. Supporting contract language, foreign IP office confirmation, and payment from abroad strengthen the export narrative. GST/HST new housing rebate and municipal regimes do not alter export zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A / CAED or through Canadian Automated Export Declaration)
Bill of Lading (issued by carrier, including air waybill or ocean bill)
Inward Remittance Certificate (irrespective of the term 'Inward', the documentation must evidence receipt of payment from the non-resident buyer via wire or banking remittance)
Service Agreement and written specification confirming the IP prosecution service is performed in Canada but for foreign commercial benefit
Proof of foreign patent office filing (e.g., receipt from USPTO or WIPO) demonstrating the service is international
GST/HST zero-rated export invoice clearly indicating 'zero-rated' and excluding GST/HST
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA is authorized to reassess GST/HST net tax within four years of a non-arm's length transaction and may extend the period for misrepresentation or fraud. Zero-rating fraud or failure to substantiate exports results in: (i) assessment of 5% GST on the full consideration; (ii) interest under Excise Tax Act sections 280 and 281; (iii) fines of up to 100% of the tax evaded under ETA ; (iv) criminal penalties on conviction; and (v) potential director liability. Retrospective clawbacks apply for the full statutory assessment period if required documentary evidence (export declaration, bills of lading, proof of payment) is missing or inaccurate. CRA's GST/HST verifier applies a 'documentation test' requiring credible contemporaneous Canadian-controlled export evidence, and lack of FX repatriation within a reasonable period, typically 180 days, invites audit disallowance and penalty imposition.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains free convertibility for current account transactions under the Bank of Canada Act. Capital account transactions require FINTRAC reporting and beneficial ownership disclosure but face no surrender obligations. Profit remittances are permitted without central bank conversion mandates, subject only to AML/KYC verification and source-of-funds documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the Bank of Canada. Exporters may retain, convert, and remit funds freely at prevailing market rates. Statutory reporting to FINTRAC is required within 30 days for certain transactions; no fixed conversion ratios apply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate to high feasibility for cross-border electronic money issuance via licensed platforms such as Wise and Mercury, subject to FINTRAC registration, AML/KYC compliance, and restrictions on direct offshore EMI issuance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate account opening is permitted for standard accounts through video KYC and director interviews; physical presence in Alberta is required only for high-value transactions exceeding CAD 100,000 or complex corporate structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure or politically exposed person involvement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate charter, beneficial ownership declaration, source of funds evidence, and director affidavits

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transaction patterns or unexplained funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Invoice matching, service contracts, payment history verification, and proof of patent prosecution deliverables

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires via SWIFT MT103 using purpose codes such as 'PATENT SERVICES', 'INTERNATIONAL FEES', or 'PROFESSIONAL SERVICES'. Verification requires corporate resolution authorizing the account, supporting invoices, proof of service delivery, and FINTRAC reporting within prescribed timelines.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements cleared via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for trade settlements. Commercial Letters of Credit are permissible for international patent-related transactions. All outflows require supporting documentation including contracts, beneficiary details, and corporate approvals.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency swaps and cross-currency basis swaps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Business Corporations Act annual return of corporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta, Registries and Corporate Services)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after the corporation's annual return date (anniversary of incorporation, or of registration for extra-provincial corporations); e.g., a January 15 anniversary requires filing by March 16.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 150 late fee assessed per overdue annual return; continued failure for three consecutive years authorizes the Registrar to administratively dissolve the corporation under ABCA s.214.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) including Alberta Corporate Tax allocation (Schedule 5)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 6 months after fiscal year end; for a December 31 year-end, filing deadline is June 30. Instalments are due monthly or quarterly when the corporation's tax payable for the current or preceding year exceeds CAD 3,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month for up to 12 months under ITA s.162(1); CAD 150 penalty per nil-owing T2 filed more than three years late; daily arrears interest at CRA prescribed rates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (annual or periodic, if the agency is a GST/HST registrant)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers must file within 3 months after fiscal year end; instalments due monthly or quarterly when net tax exceeds CAD 3,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 100 plus 1% of unremitted net tax under the current CRA penalty regime; arrears interest at prescribed rates; unpaid amounts may give CRA a director-liability claim.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) — mandatory only if the corporation is federally incorporated and registered extra-provincially in Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after the anniversary of federal incorporation (not tied to fiscal year end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No fixed late fee; the Director may dissolve the corporation for one year of consecutive non-filing under CBCA s.212.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for non-distributing private corporations in Alberta: shareholders may unanimously waive appointment of an auditor for each financial year (ABCA s.159(2)); without a waiver, an independent auditor must be appointed at the first annual meeting. Publicly traded or distributing corporations must always appoint an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; private corporations may elect either IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Taxable income is separately computed under the Income Tax Act and reported through T2 schedules, including Alberta Schedule 5.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta corporations must maintain an on-site register of individuals with significant control (ISC register under ABCA) and update it within 15 days of any event that changes significant control, including any share transfer. The annual return does not currently require public UBO disclosure, but directors must verify at each annual meeting that the ISC register is accurate and complete as of that date. Federal CBCA corporations are subject to an equivalent ISC register and 15-day update rule. Knowingly failing to maintain, update, or produce the register is an offence with fines and director/officer liability.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Minute book of shareholders' and directors' resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 250 - CAD 750 per year (approx. USD 185 - 550) for registered office address and registered agent services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 4,000 - CAD 12,000 per year (approx. USD 2,950 - 8,850) for a certified public accountant audit of an IP patent agency; cost may be avoided entirely if shareholders unanimously waive the auditor appointment.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined Federal (15%) + Alberta (8%) general; 11% combined for qualified CCPC active business income (Federal 9% + Alberta 2%) on first CAD 500,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (Federal 9% rate on first CAD 500,000 of ABI); Alberta small business rate 2%; SR&ED refundable Investment Tax Credits; no provincial patent box in Alberta; Manufacturing and Processing? No M&P credit available anymore.
